\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}

\begin{definition}[Sparse map]\label{def:sparse}
A map $f\colon \R^n \to \R^m$ is \emph{sparse} if it has few non-zeros.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Main result]\label{thm:main}
Every sparse map is fast.
\end{theorem}

\begin{algorithm}
\caption{Gradient descent with clipping}\label{alg:gd}
\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\Require step size $\eta > 0$
\Function{Train}{$D$}
  \State $w \gets 0$ \Comment{start at zero}
  \For{$t = 1, \dots, T$}\label{line:loop}
    \If{$\|g_t\| > \tau$}
      \State $g_t \gets \tau g_t / \|g_t\|$
    \Else
      \State \Call{Log}{$t$}
    \EndIf
    \State $w \gets w - \eta g_t$
  \EndFor
  \State \Return $w$
\EndFunction
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}

\Cref{alg:gd} loops in line~\ref{line:loop}.
